title: Murder charge filed months after deadly Taylorsville fight - NewsBreak
text:
By Sorina Trauntvein ,
8 hours ago
Charges are allegations only. All arrested persons are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
TAYLORSVILLE, Utah ( ABC4 ) — The two men arrested following a deadly fight in July have now been charged. The fight occurred in the early hours of July 5 in Taylorsville.
Miguel Angel Rivera, 34, is charged with murder, a first-degree felony. Juan Jose Perez Rivera, 37, is charged with aggravated assault resulting in loss of consciousness and obstruction of justice, both second-degree felonies.
According to court documents, on July 5, Taylorsville Police officers responded to a fight in progress. When they arrived, police discovered a man lying on the ground with blood pooled around him and his leg seriously injured.
Life-saving measures were attempted, but ultimately the man was pronounced dead. The victim was identified as 44-year-old Luis Ramirez.
PREVIOUSLY: Two men arrested after Taylorsville fight turns deadly A witness told police that on that night, she was at her house with Ramirez and two friends. The group was on the back patio drinking alcohol. Just after 2 a.m., she received a text from one of her friends saying that someone was at the front door and to let him in.
When the witness opened the door, she was met by a group of three men, one of whom had been invited and two others, who were later identified as Miguel Rivera and Perez Rivera. One of her friends then came to the front door and told the three that “the party was over” and “he wasn’t going to let them inside.”
The group allegedly became upset, and one of the men threw a full can of beer through the front window of the house, causing it to break. Ramirez went outside with his friends to confront the group and threw a rock through the window of their BMW.
A fight ensued in the street, during which the victim was knocked to the ground unconscious after being punched by Perez Rivera. The man with Miguel Rivera and Perez Rivera told them repeatedly that they should go and was not involved in the fight, witnesses said.
Miguel Rivera, Perez Rivera, and the man with them got into the purple BMW and backed out of the driveway. One witness saw that the victim might get hit, and threw a glass bottle at the vehicle, and tried to get them to stop. As Ramirez’s friends were attempting to move him off the street, the BMW allegedly accelerated and ran over him.
FIRST STORY: One dead after fight at Taylorsville home After police arrived, detectives searched the area and located a key fob that appeared to belong to the BMW. Through their investigation, detectives reportedly learned that the vehicle was registered to Perez Rivera.
An autopsy performed on the victim by the Utah Medical Examiner’s Office showed that Ramirez was killed by blunt force injuries, and the manner of death was homicide.
A search warrant was served on Perez Rivera’s home in Davis County, where officers allegedly located a purple BMW inside the garage with a broken back window and rear driver’s side window.
Another search warrant for inside the BMW allowed officers to locate evidence such as fibers, hair, a bloody undershirt, and a green whiskey bottle. Shortly before serving the warrants, police saw a Buick leave the residence.
Law enforcement conducted a traffic stop on the Buick, and Perez Rivera and Miguel Rivera were allegedly found inside. During the stop, Perez Rivera allegedly told Miguel Rivera to “shut up” and “don’t say anything.”
How to make ABC4 your preferred news source on Google The man who was with Perez Rivera and Miguel Rivera on the night of the deadly fight later told police that he had first met them after detailing Perez Rivera’s purple BMW. On the night of July 4, Miguel Rivera picked him up because Perez Rivera was already drunk. The group allegedly went to a fireworks show and was then invited to the residence where Ramirez was.
When they arrived, Miguel Rivera and Perez Rivera were allegedly denied entry because “they were drunk and aggressive.” The man told police that Perez Rivera threw a rock at the front window, and a fight followed.
After Ramirez was knocked unconscious, the three loaded back into the BMW, and Miguel Rivera was driving. The man said that he felt the vehicle go over the victim and then sped away. He asked Perez Rivera and Miguel Rivera to let him out because he wasn’t involved, and they dropped him off a few blocks away.
Later, the man who was with Miguel Rivera and Perez Rivera that night received a text from Ramirez’s friend that he had died. Perez Rivera then called him and stated that “if he told the police anything,” they would “come after him on the streets.” He took it as a death threat and began planning to move so Perez Rivera couldn’t find him.
Days after the deadly fight, both Miguel Rivera and Perez Rivera were arrested and booked into jail. Warrants have been ordered to hold them without bail.
